properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/05/2023 to MTN V OIL & GAS INC in Kittanning Township, Armstrong county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: MTN V OIL & GAS INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/30/2023
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8157505
Permit API: 005-27116
Unconventional: No
County: Armstrong
Municipality: Kittanning Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/05/2023
Comments: On Wednesday, 8/30/2023, I conducted a follow up inspection of the Mountain V Oil and Gas, Inc. P and N Coal, et al, 1 well, permit number 005-27116. The well is located in the woods off of Dam Road in Kittanning township, Armstrong county. Inspection #3580553, conducted on 7/6/2023, noted that the site access road had E and S issues that needed to be addressed. The E and S BMP's had not been maintained and surface water runoff was not being properly conveyed away from the site. This resulted in multiple areas of standing/ponded water. Inspection #3591431, conducted on 7/26/2023, noted that the operator had dug in turnouts to drain the specific areas of standing/ponded water and placed stone/gravel to stabilize these locations. These actions were minimal and areas that are not stabilized remained. The operator has placed more gravel on the access road in an attempt to stabilize, but has not re-installed the E and S BMP's along the access road and surface water runoff is still not being conveyed away from the access road. The operator's failure to re-install the E and S BMP's in order to prevent erosion and maintain stabilization on the access road has resulted in violation being cited. Violations of 25 PA Code 78.53, 25 PA Code 102.4(b)(1), 25 PA Code 102.11(a)(1), and 25 PA Code 102.22(a) are being cited for this inspection.

Violation ID: 8272184
Permit API: 051-24270
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/22/2026
Comments: On April 22 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3265061 of the OGM 1 OG Well.The findings were as follows:At the time of inspection, site ID sign (Act 9) was installed at the access road. The access road appeared stable with no observed accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns. The well appeared equipped for production. No fluid leaks are observed around the well head and associated equipment. A well tag was present, however appeared to have incorrect operator information. Additional comments and violations regarding the well tag are documented under inspection report 4188085. The GPU appeared to be in sound condition with no fluid leaks or discharges observed.In the Department's previous inspection on 5/15/2025 (IR 3979004), elevated conductivity readings were obtained in an area of a suspected release near the production tank. In a follow up inspection conducted by the Department on 11/3/2025 (IR 406739) a roll of dumpster from McCutcheon Enterprises was on site and appeared to be full. There appeared to be fresh gravel in the location of previously elevated conductivity readings/suspected release area. The Department obtained conductivity readings in similar locations of the previously elevated readings and obtained readings of 0.05mS, 0.09mS, and 0.07mS. These readings were comparable/lower than the background conductivity reading of 0.14mS.At the time of today's inspection, the previously observed roll off dumpster appeared to be removed from the site. Conductivity readings in the locations of previously elevated readings appeared comparable to the readings obtained in the Department's 11/3/2025 inspection with readings of 0.06mS, 0.10mS, and 0.05ms obtained.The Department received a response from the operator on 5/29/2025 stating: "We will inspect site and check soil for possible need of removal". The Department has not received any further communication regarding remediation of the release.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for/or how remediation of the release was conducted. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection violations under IR 3265061 will remain outstanding for the release pending receipt and review of the requested information.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Compliance Schedule Evaluation
Inspection Date: 3/23/2026
Comments: On March 23, 2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation of Diversified's Benninger 11 plugged well site located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following IR 4058495 where violations were issued for failure to comply with an order of the Department for failing to submit a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) within 60 days of restoration.According to Department records, this well was plugged on 5/14/2024, therefore the well site should have been fully restored by 2/14/2025 and a WSRR submitted no later than 4/15/2025.On 7/25/2024, the Department received a WSRR submission, however it was denied in IR 3876088 for an unrestored access road, during IR 3876088, the Department requested clarification from the Operator on whether the access road is proposed to remain. A WSRR was resubmitted on 5/29/2025 and on 9/23/2025, (documented in IR 4058495), the Department returned that WSRR due to Section E being filled out incorrectly. Permit API: 053-27204
Unconventional: No

Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-20
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed through a culvert under the access road and continued to spread out and flow through vegetation approximately 400 feet. Moody & Associates has been employed to coordinate the clean-up of this crude oil release. Jordan Sipos, P.G. completed the testing to establish the extent of the release and contaminated soil. Clean-up of the contaminated soil appears to be completed. Soil removal has been extended several hundred feet north of the area originally flagged as showing oil contamination from the release. Four piles of contaminated soil have been secured adjacent to the clean-up area until testing has been completed for disposal. A temporary road has been stoned to access the area and for the eventual removal of the contaminated soil. Manifest for the removal and disposal of the contaminated soil need to be submitted to the Department to lift the violations associated with this release. The removal of the contaminated soil was completed with the least disturbance possible to the surrounding vegetation and without creating a muddy unstable area. Replacement of topsoil and vegetation of this area needs to be coordinated with landowner and State Forest representatives. 15 Day initial Response Letter received July 1, 2019 for Alternate Remediation provision found in the PA DEP Oil and Gas Spill Policy. The report for the clean-up and restoration of the area needs to be submitted to the Department and approved before violations can be lifted.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/12/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 78.64(a) - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For a tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/12/2026
Violation Code: 78.64(a) - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For a tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112.
Violation ID: 8284376
Permit API: 123-46784
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/12/2026
Comments: Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) reported a release of produced fluids at TMP's Brown Hill Road tank battery. The tank battery consists of five 210 bbl stock tanks (# 1053, 1054, 1055, 1056, 1057), a separator, gas meter, burner, and buried brine tank. The Brown Hill Church Lease, Lyszaz Lease, and R Brown Lease are plumbed to this tank battery.It was reported that lightning from recent thunderstorms must have struck the tanks, ignited combustible contents, and caused an explosion that expanded and ruptured four out of the five tanks. The released fluid flowed through the ruptures and into the secondary containment area. It was reported that at the time of the release, the stock tanks were mostly empty but did contain some sludge from prior storage of produced fluids.Brian Bennett of TMP was onsite at the time of this inspection to discuss cleanup expectations with Evan Bruce (WQS) and I (Mathew Haemer - WQS). Brian estimated that the volume of the released fluids was approximately 4 bbl. Brian explained that he had been working on mixing sawdust with the sludge that had filled the containment area and had begun to remove the saturated sawdust to temporary storage in barrels staged inside the secondary containment area.At the time of this inspection, the buried brine tank was nearly empty. The majority of the release pooled around the buried brine tank. Brine was not reported to be a suspected component of this release. However, elevated SPC readings were observed both in the sawdust/sludge mixture (5,350 uS/cm) and in the soils of the secondary containment area's western end (8,900 uS/cm).Two groundhog holes were observed in the northwest corner of the secondary containment area. Elevated SPC readings (4,140/12,250 uS/cm) were observed in the soil inside of the groundhog holes. This indicates that at one point in time, brine discharged into the secondary containment area rose to a level sufficient to spill over into the holes, and from that point migrate outside of containment. A storage yard has been constructed downslope of the tank battery. HDPE pipe is scattered at one end, and spare pump jacks at the other. Coincidentally, the soil is visibly wet beneath the area where the HDPE pipe is scattered. Elevated SPC of soils (1,468 uS/cm) was observed where the pipe is scattered. The disturbed earth above the pipe and pump jacks also had elevated SPC readings (1,346 uS/cm). A violation for failure to construct and maintain a method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112 is being cited due to the evidence that brine was able to migrate through the secondary containment wall via the groundhog holes and/or through permeating the earthen containment.The quantity of the release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold set forth in the Department's spill policy, therefore either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required. It is requested that the source and extent of the release be identified.

Comments: On 8/10/2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection at the former location of the Lawrence Paper 1 well site in Wharton Township, Fayette County. The well was plugged on 4/21/2026, according to the Certificate of Well Plugging (COWP) submitted by the operator. Therefore, the well site should be fully restored by 1/21/2027 and a well site restoration report be submitted to the Department no later than 3/21/2027.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:The former access road is a shared landowner road that is to remain unrestored. Earth disturbances related to well plugging operations appear to be complete and the site is undergoing post plugging restoration. The Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) has been removed from the site entrance. The former well site is exhibiting approximately 40% vegetative growth coverage that lacks uniformity. There are large areas of exposed soil were observed on site, with minimal seed and mulch applied (Photos 15, 20, and 21). The Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan is on site (Photos 12, 13, and 25). The Compost Filter Sock (CFS) appears to be installed on site in accordance with E and S plan drawing and appears to be adequately maintained. No equipment relating to production and/or well plugging was observed on site. No evidence of a surface spill, such as staining and/or distressed vegetation, was observed at the location of the plugged well. Department OGI noted in IR 4208291 that the plugged well is equipped with a buried plugging monument. However, a surface marker is also present that displays the API number (Photos 22 and 23).Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to implement adequate seed and temporary stabilization on areas that were disturbed by well plugging operations.The last outstanding violation issued in IR 4179103 will be closed in IR 4257291.

Violation ID: 8179837
Permit API: 117-21652
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/14/2024
Comments: On 3/14/2024, Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection at the Watkins Unit 820 well site located in Chatham Twp, Tioga Co. This was in response to spill notification CID# 378902 of a release of produced water and oil-based mud to a 40'x40' section of the pad surface. The release was reported as coming from the annulus of a plugged well on site.It was 55 degrees and clear when I arrived on site. I met up with DEP inspectors, Lester Tayler and Scotty Brown. Prior to my arrival, Lester received the following information from Seneca's Rick Dake: Rick discovered the release on 3/14/2024 at 1500 hours. Fluid was on the pad surface and was spitting out and leaking from the 13x9 annulus of the Watkins 25H plugged OG well. Rick explained the release as being caused by rainwater flowing across the pad and into the 25H well cellar. The rainwater flowed down the annulus and pushed the lighter weight oil-based mud to surface. During the inspection, I did witness a crew using two excavators and a small front-end loader to scrape the area north and east of the 25H well cellar of loose gravel. The gravel they were scraping was wet and dark colored. The pad surface was void of water puddles and was a lighter color. This excavation area extended approximately 40' from the south side of the well cellar to the north with production equipment limiting the extent of the excavation. Dark staining marked the pad surface as the release spread on an eastward path to the riprap lined channel below the cut slope on the east side of the pad. I did witness dark brownish black blobs of liquid floating on water within the riprap channel. 3-inch boom absorbents had been placed within the riprap lined channel at the north and south extents of the visible contamination. The distance between the north and south booms was approximately 50 feet.Miller Environmental Group was on site providing cleanup activities to the site. Miller's project manager, Ernie Ginoble, said that he had responded to the site at 1500 on 3/13/2024 and provided initial response actions while assessing the scene. The cleanup crew mobilized equipment to the site on 3/14/2024 at 0630. He said that they were scraping down approximately 6 inches to a cemented layer of the pad. They were placing the excavated material into plastic-lined rolloff dumpsters that were being staged on secondary containment on the southwest corner of the pad. Prior to my leaving, they had filled three dumpsters with two more available at the site. A vac truck was on site sucking up free liquids from the pad surface and from the 25H well cellar. A vac box arrived at the site during the inspection to allow for additional volume.There is a house and a farm north of the property and houses south of the property. I did not witness any residential property to the east or to the west. The area is pasture type grasses. There is a stream across the road to the west.This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 57(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b). The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c).During a phone conversation after the inspection, Seneca's Jeff Passerrello did report that Seneca will pursue Act 2 for the release.I departed the site at 1350 hours.

Comments: Inspection 2 of 2On 06/03/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the NV55HS Well Site following receipt of a spill report. The spill was reported to the Department on 06/02/2025 at 10:58am (CTS 389543). I was accompanied by Bruce Carpenter of CNX. Additional CNX representatives and SPSI were on site. The spill was reported to have occurred on 06/02/2025 at 7:30am. It was reported that produced water sprayed under the pad from one of the valves on the GPU. The release was contained and an unknown quantity was reported. No waterways were affected. The following was observed:Behind the GPU, a seep is present. Flow from this seep has allowed water to pool on the pad. This area was actively being vacuumed to remove any production fluid within the area. Absorbent materials were in use on site (Photos 1-3).Conductivity readings in the pooled area on the pad ranged from 375 uS/cm - 9.94 mS/cm (Photos 4-9).The water leads to a collection box on the pad, that outlets downslope of the pad. The shut off valve had been closed after the spill. No elevated conductivity was noted at the outlet off pad (Photos 10, 11).The operator updated the Department on 06/05/2025 that spill remediation has been completed. The Department requests an updated estimation of amount of fluid spilled. The Department also requests that a waste manifest be submitted as soon as possible. Due to the current estimated amount of fluid released being 4-5 gallons but threatening pollution to the Waters of the Commonwealth, and reporting the spill later than 2 hours after discovery, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being issued.

Comments: On 12/12/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the GH5 well site following an incident report submitted to the Department on 12/11/2023 (376984). I was accompanied by Andrew Perine of CNX. Additional representatives from CNX, Pine Belt Energy Services, and Penn E and R onsite.I contacted the operator on 12/11/2023 to follow up on the incident. The material involved was brine water. There is a pipeline off of CNX's GH 5 well site; the drip leg for the site was next to the pipeline and they believe that is the source of the spill. The leak is on the pad and goes downhill approximately 100 feet and is approximately 20 feet in width. The spill did not make it to the stream below. The stream downslope of the spill area is Lightner Run along Lightner Run Road. The operator was waiting for dumpsters to arrive on site at the time. They had the spill isolated and the clean-up crew from Pine Belt Energy Services is on-site. They roughly estimated the spill to be 84 gallons, however at that moment, they are unsure of the extent of the spill depth-wise. The operator is going to follow Act 2 guidelines and have their third-party crew analyze the site. The following was observed during inspection on 12/12/2023:Excavation of impacted material was occurring and waste placed into lined dumpsters. At the time, two barrels were estimated to have been excavated. The labels not updated to site - I recommend that the labels are updated (Photos 1, 2).Silt fence added below impacted area. I recommend that routine maintenance is performed on fence to ensure proper placement. Some parts of fence slumping (Photo 3).The impacted area was outline with orange paint (Photos 4-6). The area was approximately 80 feet in length and 12 feet in width further down slope (Photo 6). Closer to the well, another area was marked in orange and was approximately 20 feet in length (Photos 14-16, 25).Conductivity readings were taken within the impacted area. The noted readings ranged from 0.09 m/S - 19.29 m/S (specific locations noted in photo captions). Higher reading moving up the slope and in the area of origin near the well site (Photos 7-24). They estimated that the impacted material towards the bottom of the slope was around two inches in depth and deeper towards the top of the slope. Two feet were dug to reach the impacted material. There is a stream called Lightner Run that is on the opposite side of Lightner Run Road, below the impacted area. The road is approximately 335 feet southwest (below) of the silt fence and the stream is approximately 430 feet southwest (below) of the silt fence. Penn E and R is going to take samples within the stream.Due to the release of production fluid over a barrel, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted following a reported release of produced fluid to the pad surface from 3/1/24. A workover rig is in operation drilling out plugs on the well pad following fracing operations. Equipment for the frac has mostly been removed from the location. Additional equipment was being hauled away during this inspection. I met with EQT company man Marc McCartor at the beginning of this inspection. The area of the pad surface which was impacted by the 3/1/24 release appeared dry without any visible staining. Fluid is present in the stormwater channel along the northwest pad edge. The fluid is present in the channel from the approximate halfway point of the pad edge to the compost filter sock infiltration berm at the west corner of the pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid is 4.46 mS/cm near the halfway point of the pad edge. Approximately 25 feet west within the channel, the EC peaked at 10.23 mS/cm and then gradually decreased as it headed farther west within the channel. The EC of the fluid where the path of the fluid ended at the compost filter sock berm at the west corner is 2.43 mS/cm. I notified the company man about the elevated EC fluid in the stormwater channel and then took sample 0718-237 from the fluid in the stormwater channel at 1242. The sample was sent to the state laboratory on the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. I left a voicemail for EQT representative Rick Hall at 1338 on the same day to let him know of my findings. Later that day at 1555 I spoke with EQT representative Zac Subra. He told me that an internal investigation found that a contractor was flushing lines which had contained produced fluid following fracing operations. The contractor released what they believed to be freshwater which actually contained some portion of produced fluid. Mr. Subra said that they believe that this was the origin of the fluid in the channel and that EQT intends to pursue Act 2 remediation for this release. He also stated that a vacuum truck was already on site removing the fluid with elevated electrical conductivity. He said Penn E and R and Tobias Excavation was en route to the site to characterize and excavate the impacted material, respectively. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Violations noted for this release against permit 081-21946.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21938 for the 3/1/24 produced fluid release.

Comments: On February 27, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection on the Hillview Cemetery 2 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3872789, where violations were issued against severe rutting observed onsite and for failure to post the API number and operator's information onsite. No response of any kind to IR 3872789 has been received from the operator as of the date of this inspection. NOV response was requested from the operator no later than December 9, 2024.The following was observed:The areas of significant rutting that were previously observed in the access road and well site remain (see photos 1, 2, and 4). The most severely rutted portion in the access road is situated approximately 100 feet from slate Creek, and therefore may continue to pose the potential to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth (see photo 3). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 5). The brine tank is disconnected from the well equipment at the time of inspection (see photo 6). No evidence of leaks or distressed vegetation was observed where the disconnected line is located. The brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection, with no staining or distressed vegetation on the ground around it (see photos 7 and 8). The API number and a means to identify and/or contact the operator have not been posted onsite since the time of IR 3872789. What appears to be sedimentation was observed immediately downslope of the area of most severe rutting in access road (see photo 9). It does not appear to have reached the Waters of the Commonwealth.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued under IR 3872789 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since IR 3872789 was conducted.The Department recommends that the brine tank is removed from site if it is no longer in use for production, in accordance with OGA3216(C).

The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead surface casing valve is closed, lower right side production tubular valve cracked open to port with closed valve to port and plumbed to drip/domestic house gas meter run, valve closed to stuffing box before meter and valve closed after meter to supply, production tubular left side valve is closed, upper production tubular is plumbed with no valve unions, and the production tubular plumbed on left side (opposite meter) of head to sales/surface equipment with closed valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photos #3 and #4). Meter reading and closed supply valve (photo #5). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. Some trace to moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility and one 50 bbl poly tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #6). Valve closed on main tubular feeding facility and closed valves to and from separator (photo #7). No production chart recording apparatus present (photo #8). No Well posting signage is affixed anywhere at or near facility. Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment. Oil staining present at facility on ground near separator with in the containment (photos #6 and #7). Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add permanent well posting signage to be affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 0 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021, 2020, 2019, 2018, and 2017 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2015 of 25.55 Mcf recorded over 336 days. This well continues to not be in production with valves closed (shut-in) at the wellhead to sales/production and to plumbed meter run before and after meter. Additionally, the main valve to facility is closed and there is not production recording chart apparatus at facility. This well has not reported production in over five years. This is not an active, producing well. The well is abandoned. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for well abandonment OGA3220(A).

Violation Code: OGA3259(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Drilling, altering or operating a well without a permit. Failure to comply with rules or regulations adopted under the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, DEP order, or a term or condition of the well permit.
Violation ID: 8248469
Permit API: 083-53759
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Foster Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/11/2025
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to monitor the progress of cleanup efforts undertaken at the tank battery located near the Warrant 4917 4917 156 OG well. First America Energy (FAE) is following a written plan submitted to the Department on December 19, 2024 in response to the October 28, 2024 COA between FAE and the Department.At the time of this inspection, an excavator was staged within the secondary containment area of the tank battery. The stock tanks previously located inside the secondary containment have been removed and staged nearby the 4917 156 conventional well.Evidence of excavation and soil removal was visible along the western dike of the secondary containment, and three "test holes" as referenced in the written plan are visible outside of the secondary containment area, along with surface excavation of soils. A stockpile of contaminated soil was located inside of the secondary containment.An area of elevated specific conductance was located in soils within the secondary containment area at the time of this inspection (Image 4). Jason Okerland was notified by phone on 09/11/2025 and further excavation was requested. It is expected that FAE adhere to their written plan and remove all soils with elevated specific conductance at the Warrant 4917 tank battery. It is also expected that FAE conduct confirmatory sampling of the impacted area to demonstrate attainment of remediation standards, and provide documentation of the proper disposal of all contaminated soils.At the time of this inspection, the Department has not yet received a Final Report from FAE.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/19/2024
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Nichols A (1H) well site located in Smithfield Township, Bradford County on 8/19/2024 at 1110 hours. The weather was 67 degrees F with cloudy skies. Rain fell onsite within the past 24 hours.This inspection was conducted to summarize site remediation efforts completed by Blackhill Energy after a release was reported to the DEP on 7/29/2024 and violations were cited in inspection report #3804993. Pad material/soils located within the excavation area today were field measured for electrical conductivity and ranged from 0.08 to 0.23mS/cm. No pooled fluids were located within the excavation area, however, pooled fluids on the pad surface near the excavation area were field measured for electrical conductivity and ranged from 155 to 275us/cm. No evidence of any portion of the release remaining was observed today. On behalf of Blackhill Energy, Moody and Associates (Moody's) submitted a 15-day interim report and NOV (notice of violation) response to the DEP on 8/7/2024. The report is attached to this inspection via file and has been uploaded to eFACTS. The NOV response indicated that interim remedial actions and site characterization activities were initiated on 7/29/2024. The NOV response also indicated that impacted pad materials and soils with electrical conductivity readings above 1.0mS/cm were excavated and placed in a lined roll-off container. Moody's collected soil attainment samples for the PADEP brine list and Ethylene Glycol following the PADEP's systematic random sampling protocol. Due to the presence of foam released with the produced water, Ethylene Glycol was added to the analyte list. Blackhill Energy plans to submit a Statewide Health Standard Site Characterization and Final Report within 90 days.Violations cited on 7/29/2024 against API #015-21167 remain outstanding at this site from the previous release. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has been confirmed.I departed the site at 1215 hours.

Violation ID: 8269638
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/01/2026
Comments: On 04/01/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County. The weather was 55 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last 24 hours. I arrived at 0930 hours. The DEP met with Repsol representative Ralph Babcock onsite. We traveled the area of the impact together. There are still two 24/7 water trucks onsite actively recovering fluids. Fluids above the release point were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~1080 us/cm (1 us/cm = 0.001 mS/cm) (photo #2). Those fluids continued traveling through the stormwater ditch into the active sumps (photo #3 and 4). They have excavated up to feet of material was removed from the ditch. The EC of fluids within the sump #1 and 2 was ~1.2 mS/cm. At that time Repsol instructed the truck operator to move his hoses below the sumps to start recovering those fluids which measured ~3.10 mS/cm (photo #5). The EC of the fluids that were directly entering the stormwater basin were ~540 us/cm. The stormwater basin has a containment in place (photo #7). Fluids were being recovered on top of and below the containment. ~60 barrels had been recovered today from the stormwater basin and sump #3. The EC of the fluids directly downgrade of the stormwater basin outlet and before sump #3 was ~5.1 mS/cm. The EC of fluids located below sump #3 was ~6.38 mS/cm. Brow/black vegetation was observed in that area (photo #11 and 12). We traveled downstream and the EC of the fluids were ~1.4 mS/cm. A spring intercepted the path of the flow from above grade. The EC of the fluids downstream of the spring was ~1.2-1.4 mS/cm. The EC of the marsh area was ~1.5 mS/cm. The EC of the UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the impacts was 25.3 us/cm (0.0253 mS/cm). Fluids entering UNT to Rockwell Creek at the upper confluence were field measured for EC at 2.4-2.7mS/cm (photo #18). From the upper confluence of the impact to the wetland inflow EC was 185.9- 225 us/cm (0.1859 -0.225 mS/cm) (photo #19). The EC of fluids from the UNT Rockwell Creek downstream impact was 379 us/cm.Repsol stated the stimulation activities for API #015-23994, 23995, 23996, 23997 and 23998 are scheduled to begin on 04/16/2026. Violations against API #015-23994 remain open at this time. I departed at 1100 hours.

Violation ID: 8277596
Permit API: 033-25056
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Bell Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/12/2026
Comments: Routine site inspection on June 11, 2026 of plugged well 033-25056. The E and S Control Plan (ESCP) was onsite for review. The RCE remains in place. Please note, the access road and well pad have not be restored per the ESCP found onsite. No temporary stabilization was observed. No visual site inspections were found onsite as outlined in the ESCP. Compost filter sock remains in place. Please note, the ESCP calls for 32" compost filter sock, a smaller size was observed onsite. A pile of drilling pipe was observed in the middle of the well pad. In addition, a brine tank was observed just off the edge of the earth disturbance area. A spot of dead vegetation and exposed soil approximately 2' wide by 4' long was observed by the brine tank. I discovered tracks tracks in the exposed soil and chew marks on the bottom of the brine tank. I screened the area finding elevated soils >4.00 mS/cm. A soil sample was collected 3442-988 and will be sent to the Departments lab to be tested for SAC 530 plus bromine, lithium, and strontium. Fluids were still observed in the bottom of the brine tank. I notified Diversified representative Will Warfel of my findings.Violations have been cited. The Department recommends that the operator addresses site remediation of the brine leak in accordance with policy 800-5000-001 (Addressing Spills and Releases at O and G Well Sites or Access Roads).
